tools.name: search_services
tools.description: Search ON-CHAIN service records only (the few services published with set_service). For products and APIs in general, use search_products first. Returns a compact list plus next_cursor for paging. Status 'document_valid' means only that the publisher's document parsed; endpoints are unverified.

tools.name: resolve_capability
tools.description: Rank ON-CHAIN service records for a free-text need and/or capability with rule-based, explained scoring (beta). Covers only services published on chain with a valid document; most products are not among them, so start with search_products. Never contacts providers.

tools.name: get_service
tools.description: Full registry record: endpoints, claimed payment methods (price unknown), status and evidence.

tools.name: get_connection_details
tools.description: Where and how to reach the provider directly (endpoint, interface, spec link) plus warnings. Fails with INTEGRATION_PENDING when there is nothing usable. entertao's part ends here.

tools.name: search_products
tools.description: Start here. Describe what you need in plain words (e.g. 'llm inference', 'rent gpus', 'web search') and get the best-matching products built on Bittensor subnets, each with how to reach it (API base URL, docs, auth, OpenAI compatibility, MCP), the provider's stated pricing, and how to get access: wh

tools.name: compare_products
tools.description: Compare products side by side: prices the provider states (each with its source page), check status and probe latency. Give unit (e.g. usd_per_1m_input_tokens, usd_per_gpu_hour) to get matched_price, the lowest stated price in that unit; null means no price is stated in that unit (unknown, NOT free)

tools.name: get_product
tools.description: Full researched record of a product: access details, machine-readable URLs, check results, sources.

tools.name: get_access
tools.description: How to get access to a product directly at its provider: sign-up/console URL, payment methods the provider states (card, crypto, x402, gamma, ...), and for gamma the service hotkey plus a btcli mint command template you run yourself, only from an on-chain record confirmed for this product (same API

tools.name: get_access_manifest
tools.description: Machine-readable AccessManifest v1 for a product: endpoints, operations (with input schema where known), access types (free, api_key, bearer, basic, gamma, x402, ...) marked as documented, incomplete or not covered, what your human must set up, and one-time setup steps. Every fact has a source and a

tools.name: get_operation
tools.description: One documented operation of a product with its full input schema, parameters, request body, safety class and gaps, plus its exact URL and the product's access types. Use an operation_id from get_access_manifest. Describes only; call the provider yourself.

tools.name: search_endpoints
tools.description: Search individual API operations (method + path) from validated OpenAPI specs across all products, e.g. 'chat/completions' or 'gpu'. Each result names the product and its base URL.

findings.title: Description references secrets/credentials
findings.detail: Description of "get_access_manifest" references sensitive artifacts (api_key, bearer). A tool description has no reason to mention credentials.
